claims.text: The dropoff on this trip was amended after booking, so the POL-RD-01 threshold test must be re-run against the amended endpoints. The chat log records the rider writing at 20:14:33, 'sorry uncle change to bishan junction 8 instead of amk hub, i updated the pin' (MSG-00312-001), and the trip record stores dropoff_amended_at 20:14:43 with amended_optimal_distance_km 14.0 and amended_optimal_duration_min 19.0. POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-applied against the optimal route between those amended endpoints, and POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after a POL-RD-05 adjustment. The governing baseline is therefore 14.0 km, not the 12.5 km booked optimal, and the derived deviation block computed against 12.5 km is not the governing figure. The clause is runnable here and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, because amended_optimal_distance_km is non-null.

Measured against the amended baseline, the excess is the trace distance of 17.57 km less the amended optimal of 14.0 km, i.e. 3.57 km, or 25.5% of the amended optimal. That clears the establishment gate in POL-RD-01 (over 0.8 km and over 20%) but fails BOTH materiality gates — 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute. This is therefore a non-material deviation: no POL-RD-06 uplift to FULL_REFUND is available on this trip's evidence and no material-deviation conduct referral arises. The rider's own claim_text measures the trip the same way, saying 17.6 km was driven for a trip that 'should be 14'.

Even on the platform's own derived figures computed against the 12.5 km booked optimal, the excess is 5.07 km and 40.56% (EV-GPS-00312, derived.deviation.excess_km and excess_pct). Those figures sit below both materiality gates of POL-RD-01 — 8.0 km absolute and 50% of optimal — so on no view of the baseline is this a MATERIAL deviation, and the POL-RD-06 pattern machinery cannot be triggered into an uplift or a referral by treating it as one.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the driver's profile. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 260, so neither limb of POL-RD-06 is met: no 3-or-more trailing flags, and a ratio of 0.00 against a 0.05 threshold on well over the 40 completed trips the clause requires. Under POL-GEN-01 only those two fields may be used for this test; no other field on either profile may carry an adverse finding, and none is relied on here.

The refund under POL-RD-02, run against the POL-RD-05 amended route as that clause requires, is arithmetic: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the 1.00 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + zero ERP = 20.42; charged_total is 24.52; the refund is 24.52 less 20.42 = 4.10, already a multiple of SGD 0.05. That is 16.7% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND and not a FULL_REFUND, and it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. It is the figure the rider's own 'should be 14' measure produces, and it does not support the SGD 6.00 contested.

No pass-through correction can be added on top of that figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all and tolls_erp of 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so no airport surcharge is chargeable. POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting off-route ERP twice on top of a POL-RD-02 refund, and there is nothing on these lines to correct. The distance-and-time refund computed above is the whole of the money in this case.

The rider's claim is subject to the additional corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 5 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, and the excess remaining after the POL-RD-05 adjustment (25.5%) is below 30%. The only corroboration beyond the trace on this record is the driver's own chat admission of the missed Braddell exit (MSG-00312-003). The clause forbids using this factor to deny an otherwise proven claim, so it does not defeat the claim — but it does hold the rider to the measured arithmetic on the corroborated excess of 3.57 km rather than to the SGD 6.00 asserted.

The driver's chat message MSG-00312-003 ('sorry sorry i miss the exit at braddell, go one big round come back') is an admission and the driver does not dispute it. I concede that discrete error: it is a missed exit, not an unjustified route, and its distance is already comprehended within the 3.57 km excess measured against the amended optimal. That admission does not support the rider's wider contention that the whole 17.6 km was improper, and no artifact on the record measures the excess on the amended baseline any higher than 3.57 km.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the case can be ruled on it directly. It carries 145 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs fires — no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 seconds — so the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) does not arise and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not available on this trace.

I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00312-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: no traffic advisory covers this trip window. No party asserts a traffic cause — the driver's counterparty statement rests on the recorded mid-trip destination amendment, which is a field on the trip record — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this bundle and no party has invoked an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact. Under POL-RD-13 that is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction in it, and the POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is not engaged.
